title: The rundown
note: What's going on right now, in one place. The ↗ links out to the original source; the item's own text turns into a link only once it becomes a full entry here.

items.text: Nearly 400 schools across France have shut down and roughly 2,000 people — 90% of them minors — have been taken into police custody since high-school student protests over teacher shortages and crumbling buildings turned violent, with more than 100 schools reporting serious damage.

Yemen's Houthis completed a takeover of the Bab al-Mandab strait area in September, seizing a key Red Sea island and prompting the Saudi-led coalition to move to protect commercial shipping through one of the world's most important chokepoints.

Wall Street closed higher Monday — the Dow up 0.2% to 51,267.90, the S&P 500 up 0.7% to 7,773.99, and the Nasdaq up 1.05% to a record 27,477.31 — as Nvidia hit an all-time high and tech strength outweighed concerns over bond yields and oil prices.

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen, 82, of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, for proposing and helping build the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, the detector buried under Antarctic ice that discovered the first high-energy neutrinos from beyond our solar system.

A crescent Moon occults Jupiter before dawn today across the eastern and central U.S. and southern Canada — the best Jupiter occultation visible from North America since 2004 — with the magnitude -1.9 planet vanishing behind the Moon's bright limb and reappearing about 67 minutes later.

Bitcoin held near $85,500 Tuesday after more than $172 million in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours and U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs slipped back into net outflows ahead of Wednesday's Fed minutes.

PAHO's latest regional measles report counts 53,957 confirmed cases and 68 deaths across 17 countries in the Americas as of late September, though the newest two-week tally of 709 cases was a 43% drop from the prior period.

The 2026 Booker Prize shortlist is six novels — Marlon James's The Disappearers, Douglas Stuart's John of John, Elizabeth Strout's The Things We Never Say, M. John Harrison's The End of Everything, Luke Kennard's Black Bag and Rebecca Perry's May We Feed the King — with the winner announced November 9.
